einzeiler: Poet Haleh Liza Gafori discusses translating the 13th-century mystic Rumi.
kurzfassung: Host Pádraig O'Tooma speaks with poet, translator, and musician Haleh Liza Gafori about her work bringing the 13th-century Persian mystic Rumi into English. Gafori shares insights into Rumi's life, his relationship with his mentor Shams of Tabriz, and the spiritual depth of Sufism. Throughout the conversation, she recites original Persian verses alongside her vivid English translations.
stichpunkte: Haleh Liza Gafori describes Rumi as a 13th-century Persian mystic, poet, and friend to humanity who roots for human liberation from ego and dogma.
Gafori recalls hearing her father recite Rumi's muscular, rhythmically driven poetry from their balcony in New Jersey.
She recites excerpts of Rumi's work in the original Persian, highlighting internal rhymes and the traditional Ghazal form.
The conversation emphasizes Rumi's lifelong grounding in Islam, noting how Quranic quotes and the 99 names of God shape his poetry.
Gafori details the transformative meeting between Rumi and his older companion Shams of Tabriz, which catalyzed Rumi's poetic output.
Sufism is explored as a sensual, animistic, and ecstatic tradition that views the entire natural world as pulsing with divine love.
Gafori discusses her translation philosophy, prioritizing imagery, metaphor, and emotional resonance over strict adherence to original meter or rhyme.
She explains why she titled her translation volumes Gold and Water, connecting the latter to Rumi's recurring motif of the water of life.

clips.text: The guest characterizes the historical writer as an ally who actively desires human emancipation from psychological traps and rigid belief systems.

clips.hook: The challenging experiment of being human
clips.text: The discussion turns to the unmatched sincerity of the poems, which fearlessly address both the frustrations and the ecstatic heights of living as both matter and spirit.

clips.hook: Fleeing ahead of the Mongol invasion
clips.text: The historical backdrop of the poet's youth is described, noting how his family migrated amidst widespread devastation and extreme violence led by Genghis Khan.

clips.hook: Coming down from his high horse
clips.text: The pivotal encounter in the marketplace is detailed, where the established preacher abandoned his privileged entourage to converse with a ragged wanderer.

clips.hook: A deep stillness in the midst of motion
clips.text: The host marvels at the physical practice of the whirling dance, noting how a person can rotate around their own center while remaining anchored between earth and sky.

beschreibung:
Poet, translator, and musician Haleh Liza Gafori describes the revered 13th-century Persian poet Rumi as “a good pal to humanity”. As she puts it, “He's rooting for our liberation.” In this exuberant conversation recorded for the 2025 Greenbelt Festival, she reads some of her translations, and she and Pádraig Ó Tuama illuminate the life of the man known as Rumi — his intense love of all things earthly and divine, the Islamic faith and universalist vision that flow through his work, and his life-changing connection with Shams, a Sufi mystic who catalyzed Rumi’s transformation from preacher to poet.
We invite you to subscribe to Pádraig’s weekly Poetry Unbound Substack, read the Poetry Unbound books and his newest work, Kitchen Hymns, or listen to all our Poetry Unbound episodes.
Haleh Liza Ghafori is a New York City-born translator, poet, and musician of Iranian descent. Her most recent book of translations of poetry by the 13th-century mystic Rumi is entitled Water and was released in April of 2025 by New York Review Books. Her first translation of Rumi was the acclaimed Gold, released in 2022, also by New York Review Books.
